steps.description: This is a pure machine learning / mathematical experiment to probe "solution space rigidity" using small feedforward networks as probes. I will design an experiment where a function f(x) is defined with known analytical constraints (e.g., boundary conditions, symmetry constraints, or functional equations), and I will vary the number of constraints w and the network hidden width N to find the minimal N_c(w) that achieves zero violation (max absolute error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraint points. The rigidity claim is tested by observing whether N_c(w) remains small and bounded as w increases. I will implement a multi-layer perceptron in PyTorch, train it on constraint satisfaction (not data fitting), and sweep widths from 4 to 64 for w = 4, 8, 12, 16. I will report N_c(w) values and whether they saturate (rigid) or grow unbounded (fat).
